claims.summary:
I finished the runner's scheduling step but did not write output/schedule.json: the supplied batch cannot be scheduled under the current allowances.

What changed: reconcile/scheduler.py now backtracks over every route/start option (the old version took the first option per request and gave up). A call's allowance is charged at its start and every later start. tests/test_scheduling.py covers ledger replay at the cutoff, checks that the rejected retry and the timeout retry change nothing, and checks that the supplied batch is refused while a batch with one more C unit gets a schedule. All tests pass. Running `python -m reconcile.runner` on data/ exits 2 and writes nothing.

Why it fails: after replay at cutoff 9, A has 3/6/9 units free at starts 10/11/12, B 3/3/5, C 3/3/6 and D 3/5/6. spent-C stays committed against accepted-C, and the C3, A, B and D holds are still active. Each call uses exactly one of A or B, and the batch needs 14 units, which is exactly A9 + B5. The only route split that keeps C and D within 6 puts request-3 and request-5 on B and everything else on A. D then carries request-4 and request-5 (3+3), and only 5 D units are free by start 11. request-5 must start by 11, so request-4 goes at 12. That fills A at 12, so request-1 and request-2 (via AC) both have to start by 11, which needs 4 C units when only 3 are free. An exhaustive search agrees: there is no valid assignment.

To ship this batch, the customer needs to approve one more C unit available by start 11 (that gives two valid schedules), or one more A or B unit. Another option is to release the C3 hold early or split the batch. One more D unit or one more worker at 11 does not help.
